data: Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.

Energia was the rocket that redeemed the N1 — the super-heavy launcher the Soviet Union finally got right. Where the N1 exploded on all four attempts, Energia worked, lifting the Polyus payload in 1987 and the Buran orbiter in 1988. Crucially, it was a launcher in its own right, not a shuttle stack: because Buran had no main engines, Energia did the whole job of reaching orbit and could just as well have lifted other heavy payloads with no orbiter at all. It was the most powerful rocket the Soviet Union ever flew successfully — and, like Buran, it was cancelled for want of anything left to launch.

The only Soviet super-heavy launcher to fly successfully. Designed to carry the Buran orbiter or stand-alone payloads up to 100 t to LEO. Two flights: Polyus payload test (1987) and Buran orbiter (1988), both successful. Program shelved at the end of the Cold War.
Successor to Proton-K; modernised heavy lift
Modern Soyuz workhorse — carries Soyuz MS crew + Progress MS cargo to the ISS
Soviet Moon rocket; four launches all failed
The Soviet / Russian heavy-lift workhorse 1967-2012 — Salyut, Mir, Venera, Vega, Luna sample-return
